claim: V06 §3.20.2 (l.3108-3110) places each history event and each `calamityHistory` entry 'in the epoch whose span `(toYearsAgo, fromYearsAgo]` holds its years ago; one before the start is not replayed'. The last replay epoch ends at the present ('the last ending at the present (yearsAgo 0)', V06 l.911), so its span `(0, fromYearsAgo]` excludes 0: an event or a calamity at the present week — a calamity whose tick set the present week, a history event of 0 years ago — lies in no span, though it is not before the start. Under `EpochInputs.events`' own rule '(the previous epoch's week, week]' (§4.11 l.8239) that week belongs to the last replay epoch at `W_p`. One builder drops the event, another replays it in the last epoch (DR37: the dossier's present facts met exactly at the replay's end).
required_change: V06 §3.20.2: after 'holds its years ago' add ', an event at the present (0 years ago) in the last epoch, at `W_p`'; V06 §3.21's replay row adds 'an event or a calamity at the present week | replayed in the last epoch at `W_p`'; T-V6-71 adds that fixture.

claim: A rise after a fall that held a household has no defined arrivals. Since round 3, V06 §3.5.1 (1) (l.1223-1229) passes over each locked or pinned household 'for the next household below it in that order that is neither', and (4) (l.1240-1247) passes over a protected dwelling's last household under any fall that is not a dossier fall, the next household below it leaving in its place. §7.7's precedence (base l.11718-11723) does the same under a dossier fall the unlocked households can meet. After such a fall the town holds the roster's households up to the target, less those that left in a held household's place, plus the held ones above it — no longer the roster's prefix. Yet §4.11's delta demand is 'the suffix of the sequential roster between the old and the new population, §10.2 — prefix-stable' (l.7879-7881), and §10.2's AM-8 says 'a later rise reoccupies the same suffix first' (l.15300-15302). Read as written, a rise past a held household's ordinal adds it a second time while it stands, and never returns the households that left in its place, which lie below the old population. A builder reading the delta as a set (the roster's households up to the new population the town does not hold) builds a different town. V06 §3.6 (1) reads 'the delta demand's households' and states neither reading. §3.21's decline row, T-V6-5, T-V6-6 and T-V6-70 (f) stop at the fall, and no catalogue entry or combination names the decline-then-rise sequence. The path is ordinary: a locked or pinned building on the decline path of a standalone advance that falls and then rises, or a dossier that falls and recovers. A household added twice is a silent wrong count against DR7's bar.
required_change: 1. V06 §3.5.1 (1) adds, after '`households.heldByLock` —': 'A household held so keeps its place and its roster ordinal: the town then holds the roster's households up to the met count less those that left in a held household's place, plus the held ones. At every later epoch the delta demand (§4.11's suffix between the old and the new population) is read over that set — the roster's households up to the epoch's target that the town does not hold, in ordinal order, those that left in a held household's place first (§10.2's AM-8: the same suffix back first). A held household that still stands is never added twice, so the town holds exactly the roster's prefix to the target once the target reaches every held household's ordinal.' 2. V06 §3.21's decline row adds the edge 'a rise after a fall that held a household' with the outcome 'the households that left in its place return first, the held one never added twice (V06 §3.5.1 (1))'. 3. T-V6-70 (f) adds, on H-100: 'then a rise past the held households' ordinals — no household id added twice, the passed-over households back, the town's households the roster's prefix to the new target, the members summing to it within the roster tolerance (DR7's bar)'. 4. END for pipeline: §4.11's delta-demand parenthesis (l.7880) reads 'the suffix of the sequential roster between the old and the new population, §10.2 — prefix-stable, read over the households the town holds where a fall held one (V06 §3.5.1 (1)) — so no survivor's use is withdrawn by arithmetic'.

claim: §2.7's support step (3) (round 3, R3-25 (d); l. 2552-2553) releases the band's stretch under a crossing station 'from the first epoch after the raised way is removed or the spans on both sides of the station have fallen (`ruined` or `cleared`)'. V06 §3.7.2 (2) (l. 1472) and V06 §3.7.6 (5) (l. 1599-1600), with J-V6.114 and J-V6.140, release the same stretch from dismantling 'until that raised way is removed or its crossing span `dismantled`': a span has no `dismantled` state (§2.7's `spans[].state` is 'ruined'|'cleared') and, since round 2's crossing station, no span crosses the trace — the station carries a span on each side. One builder never releases the stretch, another at one span's fall, a third at both; the model's round-3 HAND-OFFS named it and V06 did not write it.
required_change: V06 §3.7.2 (2) (l. 1472): 'until that raised way is removed or the spans on both sides of its crossing station have fallen (`ruined` or `cleared`; §2.7's support step (3))'; V06 §3.7.6 (5) (l. 1599-1600): 'from the first epoch after that raised way is removed or the spans on both sides of its crossing station have fallen (`ruined` or `cleared`; §2.7's support step (3))'; J-V6.114's and J-V6.140's 'its crossing span `dismantled`' → 'the spans on both sides of its crossing station fallen (§2.7's support step (3))'.

claim: R3-08 (b) keeps VV56-r2-06 a blocker because 'every restoration that re-cuts … would draw new elements as patched repairs they never had' — the claim's first case being the restoring event's own re-cut for its new occupants. The ruled mechanism reads each element's peak from its entry week, for an element a re-cut mints ('a restoring event's included') 'that change's effective week' (V06 §3.23 (3), l. 3409–3412; decayPeak's `since`, l. 3382; V03 §5.6 (2) (b), l. 2697–2701). At the restoring event's week the level is still the run's: a `reoccupy` under its `repair` Works reads L × (1 − f(w)) from the Works' start, L the level the week before (V06 §3.23 (3)). So an element that re-cut mints (a new occupant's partition, door, furniture) is drawn DAMAGED from its first week (a `decayed` building's level lies in [1/3, 2/3]; V11's partition range 0.36–0.66) and then REPAIRED in patch material for ever once the Works lowers the level past it, its peak since entry being L; only a restoration with no Works escapes. V06 §3.23 (3) itself says only elements added 'after' the damage left are never drawn repaired, but the bars and edge rows assert the restoring re-cut's case: T-V6-76 (b) 'a reoccupy from derelict with a re-cut …: 0 added elements drawn repaired' (V06 l. 4143), V06 §3.21's decay row 'the added elements drawn as built' (l. 3274), V03 §3.13's damage-layer row 'an element a restoring re-cut … adds → drawn as built, never repaired' (l. 2094) and T-V3-39 (c) 'drawn as built, never patched' (l. 2898). The formula gives the wrong result on the common path (works on by default) and those bars cannot pass on it.
required_change: V06 §3.23 (3), after '… or a wing an `extend` adds at that change's effective week': '— save that an element a restoring event's re-cut mints (V03 §3.11: the new occupants' rooms) enters the plan, for its damage, at the week that restoration ends — its `repair` Works' FINISHED week, or the week a decay run that interrupts it begins; with no Works, the event's effective week — and is drawn as built before that week: no level the restoration lowers damages it or is its peak, so a restoration's new elements are neither damaged nor repaired, and a kept element keeps its peak'; decayPeak's `since` comment (l. 3382) adds 'for an element a restoring re-cut mints, the week that restoration ends'; §3.21's decay row reads 'the added elements drawn as built through the restoration and after it, the kept ones patched'; T-V6-76 (b) adds 'under a `repair` Works, every element the reoccupy's re-cut mints drawn as built in every week of the Works'. Ends: V03 §5.6 (2) (a) adds 'an element is compared with the level only from its entry week ((b); V06 §3.23 (3))', and (b)'s 'that change's effective week (V06 §2.11)' reads 'that change's effective week (V06 §2.11) — for a restoring event's re-cut, the week that restoration ends (V06 §3.23 (3))'; V03 §1b's and §2.5's `planDamage` input cells the same; model §2.6 step 7's 'an element that entered the plan after its damage left never drawn repaired' adds 'nor one a restoring re-cut minted (V06 §3.23 (3))'.

claim: Persists in part. R3-08 (b)'s per-element peak is written everywhere it was routed (V06 §3.23 (3) and its `since`, W94, §2.12, §6.9, §3.21, T-V6-76 (b), J-V6.139; V03 §5.6 (2) (b), V02 §5.7 (2), X34, X36, §8.6, §2.6 step 7, V10 l. 1829) and closes an `extend` after a repair and a re-cut after the damage left. It does not close the restoring event's own re-cut, the case the finding led with. V03 §3.11 (l. 2017–2021): the restoring event (a `reoccupy`, a repair) 're-cut[s] a stored plan inside that event and stale[s] an unstored one … the kept elements keeping their thresholds while the damage leaves'; V03 §5.6 (2) (b) and V06 §3.23 (3) give each element that re-cut mints `since` = 'that change's effective week (V06 §2.11)', an engine op's epoch week E (V06 l. 823). The `repair` Works the `reoccupy` starts begins at S, uniform over (prevWeek, E] (V06 §3.13 (2); §4.11 *Works* (5), (10)), and runs its drawn duration; wherever it has not reached FINISHED by E, V06 §3.23 (3) gives the level at E as L × (1 − f(E)) > 0. Every minted element (the new occupants' partitions, doors, furniture; fresh thresholds by §6.3) whose t lies at or below that level is drawn damaged from E by §6.3's comparison and, once the falling level passes below t, 'repaired, in patch material', counted in `info.damage.patched` (V10 l. 1829): the wrong result the blocker named, on a common path (every `reoccupy` re-cuts or re-derives for new occupants; Works start uniformly in the span, so any positive repair duration begun in its last weeks runs past E). T-V6-76 (b)'s property over H-100 ('a `reoccupy` from derelict with a re-cut …: 0 added elements drawn repaired') fails under the rule as written; J-V6.139's 'a per-element peak never draws as repaired an element the damage never reached' holds only by drawing the new element damaged first. `decayPeak`'s 'highest decayLevel over [since, week]' is also undefined for week < since (a frame inside the span holds the event's re-cut plan from the Works' start, V06 §3.15.2).
required_change: V06 §3.23 (3), after 'an element a re-cut keeps keeps its peak': 'An element reads the building's level — for §6.3's comparison and for `decayPeak` — only from a decay run that begins at or after its entry into the plan: an element that enters while a restoration is lowering the level (the restoring event's own re-cut, its `repair` Works still running at the event's effective week) reads 0 until the building's next decay run, so it is drawn as built through the repair and never repaired'; the signature's comment reads 'the highest decayLevel over [since, week] of the runs begun at or after `since`; 0 with none, and 0 for week < since'; §3.21's decay-level row adds 'a `reoccupy` whose re-cut is made while its `repair` Works runs past its epoch's week | the minted elements drawn as built throughout the repair, the kept ones leaving the damage and patched'; T-V6-76 (b)'s fixture names a `reoccupy` whose `repair` Works is still running at its epoch's week. At its home (END): V03 §5.6 (2) (a)–(b) read each element's level by that rule (an element minted by the restoring event's re-cut neither damaged nor repaired by the run it entered during), V02 §5.7 (2) reading it through V03.

claim: V06 §6.8 (6) (l. 3976–3981), T-V6-24 and J-V6.136 state the catch-up's over-budget branch as 'where even one epoch over the span with its events' term passes the budget'; V06 §1.1 (14) (l. 148), W91 (l. 374), §6.8's lead (l. 3918), §6.8 (3) (l. 3952–3953: 'a catch-up's fits its budget but where its dossier events alone pass it') and §3.21's dossier-bound row (l. 3253) state it as 'dossier events alone pass its budget'. They differ where the events' term is under the budget but one epoch over the span plus it is over — at the metropolis cap one epoch is ≈ 5.3 s against 6 310 ms inside an open, so about 23 events at 45 ms already pass — where (3)'s claim that one epoch then fits is false; (6) governs the build.
